reason: The text extensively emphasizes that the identity and covenantal relationship of the Hebrews/Israelites centers on their worship and service to Yahweh. Throughout the narrative, worship ('עבודה' - avodah) and serving God ('וְיַֽעַבְדֻנִי') are presented as the defining characteristics of the Hebrew people. The Passover institution, the giving of divine statutes and laws (חוקים ומשפטים), and repeated covenant language all establish that their distinctive identity as God's people is inseparable from their obligation to worship and obey God. The text repeatedly states that God's relationship to them is predicated on their recognition of Him as their God and their commitment to serve Him. Even in wilderness narratives, their identity as a distinct people is reinforced through shared religious practices and obligations to Yahweh.
